title: Permission Sculptor — compact member assignment & audit preview
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design a compact, low-friction UI for assigning team members and groups to RBAC v2 permission sets, with an inline audit preview showing recent changes and SSO group mappings. The surface must support fast common tasks (add/remove member, assign template), progressive disclosure for inheritance/granularity, and a live preview of the audit trail and required approvals before committing changes.
background: RBAC v2 introduces finer-grained permission sets and group-based bindings. Platform customers have asked for a streamlined way to update membership and bindings without navigating multiple consoles. Current patterns are verbose and force admin to context-switch to audit logs and SSO settings. This design aims to consolidate assignment, preview of effective permissions, and audit metadata into a single compact modal/workflow.
scope:
- Compact assignment modal accessible from workspace/team list and role detail pages.
- Inline effective-permission preview for selected targets (member, group, service account).
- Audit preview panel showing last 10 relevant events (who, when, change summary).
- SSO group mapping hint and link to SAML settings.
- Support for dry-run (preview-only) and staged commit with optional approver flow for tenant-admins.
Excludes: deep audit history exploration (link out), detailed SAML configuration screens, and backend change propagation logic (handled by ENG).
user_flows: Quick-add: admin opens compact modal, types or pastes email, sees inline effective permission preview, clicks Add -> success toast and brief audit entry created.
Group-assign: admin selects SSO group, sees mapped members and effective permission diff, chooses 'Assign to role', optionally marks 'Require approval' for staged rollout.
Bulk-invite: paste list of emails -> UI shows per-row validity, conflicts, and aggregated audit preview before commit.
acceptance_criteria: Compact modal prototype in Figma with accessible keyboard flow and responsive states
Effective-permission preview calculates and displays allow/deny summary for selected target (frontend stubbed with sample data)
Audit preview panel surfaces last 10 changes with actor, timestamp, and link to full audit log
Dry-run mode shows exact diffs without persisting changes
Designs handed off to ENG with component specs and interaction notes
Usability test with 6 participants shows >80% success on common tasks (add member, assign group, preview audit)
dev_notes: Frontend should call GET /v2/rbac/effective-permissions?target_id=<id> to render preview (stub available in staging)
Audit preview uses /v2/audit/events?filter=rbac&limit=10; event schema: actor, action, target, timestamp, diff-summary
SSO mapping hint links to /v2/sso/groups/:id; backend provides mapped members via /v2/sso/groups/:id/members
Staged commit uses POST /v2/rbac/changes?staged=true and returns a change_id for approval flow
Accessibility: modal must trap focus, support screen-reader announcements for success/error and provide aria-describedby for diffs
decisions: Use a right-side split layout in the modal: left for assignment inputs and selected targets, right for effective-permission + audit preview.
Show only top-level permission categories in inline preview (read/write/admin) with a 'view detailed diff' link to expand.
Default to non-approver commits for workspace admins; tenant-admins can enable 'Require approval' per change.
Bulk paste will attempt email resolution and show unresolved entries as pending invite rather than blocking the entire operation.
open_questions: Should service accounts be treated differently in the preview UI (token rotation caveats)?
How should transient errors from SSO group API be surfaced in the modal without blocking users?
Do we allow assigning a role to users that currently have a deny rule that would block effect? (edge-case conflict resolution)
Who will own the audit-preview backend rate limits if the modal is used in high-volume bulk edits?
